top_story.headline: Seafarers union PAC reports insurance recovery for 'additional misappropriations' of committee funds
top_story.dek: The FEC's October 8 letter says the $13,064.50 receipt appears related to an apparent unauthorized use of committee funds.
paragraphs: The Federal Election Commission sent an RFAI dated October 8, 2026 to Seafarers Political Activity Donation, the political action committee of the Seafarers International Union of North America–AGLIW, about its September Monthly Report. Schedule A shows a $13,064.50 receipt described as "Insurance recovery for additional misappropriations found See memo."

The Commission wrote that the receipt "appears to be related to an apparent unauthorized use of Committee funds" and that it "may take further legal action regarding this apparent improper use." The letter is addressed to the committee's treasurer, Thomas Orzechowski, Jr., and contains a single item.

Two other RFAIs dated the same day raise similar flags: Bish for Congress has debit-card "fraud charge" disbursements of $483.27 and $1,000.00 offset by $11,193.51 in Wells Fargo provisional credits, and the EchoStar DISH Network PAC reported a $4,767.41 "DISPUTED ACH DEBIT." Both letters carry the same legal-action warning.

sections.headline: Twelve filings from ten sitting House members — mostly excess-contribution and 48-hour-notice questions
paragraphs: Nine House incumbents drew eleven RFAIs dated October 8, and a tenth, Rep. Robert J. Wittman, filed a Form 99 answering an earlier RFAI. The most common issue is contributions over the per-election limit that have not yet been refunded, redesignated or reattributed.

items: Rep. Eric Swalwell (D-CA) — Swalwell for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: the Federal Election Commission notes two cash-on-hand adjustment entries labeled "Uncashed Checks - See Form 99 For Additional Information" and asks for any further detail on that adjustment as it becomes available. Filing.

Rep. Herbert C. Conaway, Jr. (D-NJ) — Herb Conaway for Congress — RFAI on the April Quarterly Report: the election-cycle-to-date (Column B) totals on lines 7(a), 7(c), 17 and 22 look wrong and must be amended, along with any later reports affected. Filing.

Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) — Torres for Congress — RFAI on an amended 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (received 07/13/2026): contributions on Schedule A appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. The letter acknowledges the committee's earlier explanation of corrective action but says one or more of the excess contributions still have not been fixed. Filing.

Rep. Thomas H. Kean, Jr. (R-NJ) — Kean for Congress Inc — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. Filing.

Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL) — Mike Haridopolos for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: transfers from Faith, Honor, & Courage look like joint-fundraising proceeds, but that committee is not listed as a joint fundraising representative on the committee's Statement of Organization, which must be amended (or the report clarified). Filing.

Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL) — Mike Haridopolos for Congress — Second RFAI, on the 12-Day Pre-Primary Report: same problem with transfers from Shoring Up Republican Futures Fund (SURF Fund), which is likewise not disclosed as a joint fundraising representative. Filing.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) — Josh for Jersey — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: the committee may have missed required 48-hour notices for contributions of $1,000 or more received just before the primary, and two "last minute" contributions from Tamara Winn on 05/14/2026 that were reported in 48-hour notices do not appear on Schedule A. Filing.

Rep. Sarah McBride (D-DE) — McBride for Delaware Inc. — RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01–08/26/2026): Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. Filing.

Rep. Zachary Nunn (R-IA) — Iowans for Zach Nunn — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: contributions on Schedule A appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. The letter notes the committee's earlier explanation of corrective action but says some excess contributions had still not been refunded, redesignated or reattributed. (The letter runs 16 pages with attachments.) Filing.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ) — LaMonica McIver for Congress — RFAI on an amended April Quarterly Report (received 05/18/2026): Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. Filing.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ) — LaMonica McIver for Congress — Second RFAI, on the July Quarterly Report: possible missed 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions of $1,000 or more; 48-hour notices that never made it onto Schedule A; and two $3,000 contributions from Joseph W. Kaempfer Jr. on 05/20/2026 of which only part is disclosed on the report. Filing.

Rep. Robert J. Wittman (R-VA) — Rob Wittman for Congress — Form 99 answering an RFAI on the July Quarterly Report about excessive and impermissible contributions: five contributions (from W Hunt, Cox Enterprise PAC (Coxpac) Inc., Employees of Onebrief Inc. It also says Main Street Virginia Political Action Committee was recorded as a state or local party committee. Filing.

sections.headline: Fifty-five RFAIs in all, headlined by two reports of apparent unauthorized spending
paragraphs: The FEC's Reports Analysis Division sent 55 RFAI letters dated October 7–8, 2026; the 44 below are to challengers, open-seat candidates and PACs or party committees (the other 11 are under Sitting Lawmakers). Most carry a November 12, 2026 response deadline. Three letters say the FEC may take legal action over apparent unauthorized use of committee funds: Seafarers Political Activity Donation, Bish for Congress and the EchoStar DISH Network PAC. The rest are routine: unsigned reports, wrong summary-page totals, negative cash balances and excessive contributions.

items: Hamawy for New Jersey — RFAI on an amended July Quarterly Report (received 08/13/2026): disbursements to Payroll Service Solutions labeled "Payroll" need memo entries naming each salary recipient (address, date, amount, purpose) once a person is paid more than $200 in the cycle. Filing.

McKay for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: reports a negative ending cash balance of $20,918.65, which suggests an overdraft, math error or unreported debt (an overdraft can be a prohibited bank contribution); and a candidate loan on Schedule C that no longer says whether it came from personal funds or a bank or credit line. Filing.
McKay for Congress — RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01–07/18/2026): negative ending cash balance of $19,055.55 and the same unexplained candidate-loan source question. Filing.

Neil for Congress — RFAI on an amended April Quarterly Report (received 06/23/2026): general-election contributions are still being held even though the candidate will not be in the general election; they must be refunded or redesignated to the primary (if there is net primary debt) within 60 days after the primary. Filing.

Neil for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: asks whether a loan from the candidate came from personal funds or from a bank, credit card or other credit line (which would require a Schedule C-1). Filing.

Mike Lipetri for Congress — RFAI on an amended 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (received 06/26/2026): contributions from organizations not registered as political committees need proof the money was permissible; the amended report also shows $43,146.87 more in vendor debt and $51,099.27 more in receipts than the original, which must be explained. Filing.
Hispanic Political Action Coalition (HISPAC) — RFAI on a Statement of Organization: no mailing address listed for the committee's campaign depository on Line 9. Filing.

Advance Liberty PAC — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: possible missed 48-hour independent-expenditure reports; 48-hour reports naming "SOUTH LAKE QUICK PRINT" whose amounts and dates do not match Schedule E; and a vague purpose, "GENERAL CONSULTING." Filing.

Young People for a New Era — RFAI on an amended July Quarterly Report (received 09/14/2026): disbursements rose $18,516.17 from the original, which the committee blamed on an upload error that left disbursements off the first version; the letter also says 24-hour reports naming "Don Mickey Designs, Inc" do not match Schedule E dates. Filing.

Rachel Grage for Congress — RFAI on the 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (07/01–07/29/2026): cycle-to-date totals look wrong, the beginning cash balance does not match the prior ending balance, and a reminder on itemizing earmarked contributions behind "Act Blue Processing Fee" payments. Filing.

Hoan for 9 — RFAI on an amended 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (received 06/23/2026): apparent credits on debt owed to Athena Design Group; the committee must say whether the debt was forgiven (only terminating committees may settle debts) or disputed. Filing.

Hoan for 9 — RFAI on an amended April Quarterly Report (received 06/23/2026): general-election contributions still held though the candidate will not appear in the general election, and possible missed 48-hour notices for last-minute contributions of $1,000 or more. Filing.
Hoan for 9 — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: negative ending cash balance of $13,997.45, suggesting an overdraft, math error or unreported debt. Filing.

U.A. Local 85 Political Action Committee — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: interest from Huntington Bank, a depository not listed on the Statement of Organization; plus operating expenditures reported on the wrong Detailed Summary Page lines. Filing.

International Association of Heat and Frost Insulators and Asbestos Workers Local No. 1 PAC — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: the report was not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on file, and it is missing its Detailed Summary Page. Filing.

Bish for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: Schedule B shows "fraud charge" disbursements of $483.27 and $1,000.00 that the FEC says appear to be an unauthorized disbursement of committee funds, and Schedule A shows Wells Fargo "provisional credits" of $5,001.21 and $6,192.30 offsetting debit-card fraud; the committee must identify the expenditures behind the offsets. The letter says the FEC may take further legal action. Filing.
Democrats Who Win — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: transfers to affiliated committees were reported on the wrong line; they belong on a separate Schedule B under Line 22. Filing.
New Voice PAC — RFAI on an amended July Quarterly Report (received 07/15/2026): Schedule A contributions flagged as apparently excessive (details in attachment to the letter). Filing.
For Our Children Florida PAC — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: possible missed 24-hour reports for last-minute independent expenditures of $1,000 or more. Filing.

America Is Back — RFAI on an amended Statement of Organization (received 09/18/2026): the form says the committee is a joint fundraising representative but also lists NRSC, "Rogers for Senate," "Sununu Senator," "Tafoya for Senate" and "Mike Collins for Senate" in both joint-fundraising and affiliated-committee lines; the committee must clarify those relationships. Filing.

The Equity Alliance Fund Action PAC — RFAI on the June Monthly Report: $10,860.00 in "voided" independent-expenditure checks was reported as a receipt on Line 15; an uncashed voided check should instead be a negative entry on Schedule E. Filing.

Reviving American Jobs Again PAC (d/b/a Equal Opportunity Now) — RFAI on the August Monthly Report: Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt, plus a second item on Schedule B disbursements. Filing.

ClearPath Action Fund, Inc. — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: negative entries on Schedule E for independent-expenditure adjustments must be explained as either report corrections or refunds (which belong on Schedule A). Filing.
Independence Blue Cross LLC PAC — RFAI on an amended August Monthly Report (received 09/17/2026): Schedule B contributions flagged as apparently exceeding limits. Filing.

Maine Republican Party — RFAI on the August Monthly Report: omitted ongoing debts to "XEROX FINANCIAL SERVICES"; a $10,000.00 transfer to what looks like a non-federal account; and Schedule H4 reimbursements of $2,171.63 against memo entries totaling only $1,382.83. Filing.

California Democratic Party — RFAI on the August Monthly Report: $12,750 in "strategic consulting services" payments to individuals on Schedule H4 (are they employees, and did they spend 25% or less of their time on federal election activity?) and a payment for "campaign finance -data imports (not an employee)." Filing.

EchoStar Corporation and DISH Network Corporation PAC (EchoStar DISH Network PAC) — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: a $4,767.41 "DISPUTED ACH DEBIT" that the FEC says appears to be an unauthorized disbursement of committee funds; the letter says the FEC may take further legal action. Filing.
EDF Action Votes — RFAI on the August Monthly Report: the independent-expenditure purpose "Production" is too vague and must be clarified on Schedule E. Filing.
Galveston County Republican Party — RFAI on the Mid-Year Report: Schedule A contributions that appear to come from corporations or LLCs taxed as corporations, which are prohibited. Filing.

Seafarers Political Activity Donation (Seafarers International Union of North America–AGLIW) — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: a $13,064.50 receipt described as "Insurance recovery for additional misappropriations found See memo," which the FEC says appears related to an apparent unauthorized use of committee funds; the letter says the FEC may take further legal action. Treasurer is Thomas Orzechowski, Jr. Filing.
Leadership for Ohio Fund — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on file. Filing.

Oregonians for Common Sense PAC — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on file, and other disbursements were reported on the wrong Detailed Summary Page line. Filing.
Halff Associates Fed PAC — RFAI on the October Quarterly Report: not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on file. Filing.
Monroe Township Republican Executive Committee — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: not signed by the treasurer or designated agent on file. Filing.

Mike Thurow for Congress — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: cycle-to-date totals on a dozen summary lines look wrong, and the beginning cash balance does not match the amended April Quarterly Report's ending balance. Filing.

Chuck Smith for US Senate — RFAI on the April Quarterly Report: Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. Filing.

Erik Murray for Kansas — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: Schedule A contributions that appear to exceed the contribution limits ($3,500 per election from an individual, $5,000 from a multicandidate committee), asking for a refund, redesignation or reattribution within 60 days of receipt. Treasurer Andrew Madras also signs for Torres for Congress. Filing.
AB PAC — RFAI on the September Monthly Report: Column B totals on lines 24 and 29 look wrong, and possible late 24-hour reports for last-minute independent expenditures. Filing.

Southern California Pipe Trades District Council 16 Federal PAC — RFAI on an amended 12-Day Pre-Primary Report (received 09/01/2026): receipts rose $26,207.02 from the original version, which must be explained. Filing.

Jewelers of America, Inc. Political Action Committee (JAPAC) — RFAI on the October Quarterly Report: contributions to candidates for the 2026 primary were disbursed after the primary date; contributions cannot be designated for a past election unless retiring debt, so the committee must seek a refund or written redesignation. Filing.

Broward Democratic Party — RFAI on a Statement of Organization: the form claims state-party-committee status, which requires an advisory opinion from the Commission before state-party contribution limits can be used. Filing.

American Pharmacists Association Political Action Committee — RFAI on an amended April Quarterly Report (received 09/23/2026): receipts rose $16,527 from the original version, which must be explained. Filing.

Building Empowerment and Accountability Now (BEAN) PAC — RFAI on an amended Statement of Organization (received 10/01/2026): the committee's name includes a federal candidate's name but it does not appear to be that candidate's authorized committee; it must change the name or clarify. Filing.
American Dreams PAC — RFAI on the July Quarterly Report: interest from Classic City Bank, a depository not listed on the Statement of Organization. Filing.

sections.headline: Thirty-three more Form 99 submissions — mostly 'under $5,000' statements, plus a $192 million presidential report
paragraphs: With the October Quarterly Report due October 15, many tiny committees filed Form 99 statements saying they have not reached the $5,000 reporting threshold. Others answer RFAIs. The oddest is a Mercer for President report listing $192 million of in-kind contributions from the candidate himself.

items: Mercer for President (presidential candidate) — Filed as a Form 3P report covering 07/01–09/30/2026 (signed by Lee Mercer), it reports $192,000,000.00 in receipts and the same in operating expenditures, all from in-kind contributions by the candidate (the first for $64,000,000.00 on 07/28/2026) with a purpose line beginning "In-kind - E.C. Hot W. Hook Up Intel Criminal Investi of the U S Gov 2028 election Citizens"; cash on hand is $3,060.78. (Filed 10/07; first surfaced in FEC data in this edition.) Filing

Jeremy Levan for President 2028 (presidential candidate) — Filing frequency change notice: switching from quarterly to monthly reporting, effective immediately. (Filed 10/07; first surfaced in FEC data in this edition.) Filing

Fight to Win — Responds to an RFAI on the July Monthly Report, explaining that the same $55,725.60 independent expenditure to The Pivot Group, Inc. (split $41,794.20 opposing Shah and $13,931.40 supporting Galan-Woods) shows different dates only because one report used the June 22 obligation date and the other the July 1 payment date, and says no amendment is needed. (Filed 10/07; first surfaced in FEC data in this edition.) Filing

Rana Abdelhamid for Congress (challenger, NY) — Responds to an RFAI dated 09/02/2026: the committee plans to spend its remaining funds on contributions to federal, state and local candidates and then terminate, and will notify the Commission if it converts to a multicandidate committee. (Filed 10/07; first surfaced in FEC data in this edition.) Filing

Andom for Congress (NY) — Disavowal response: Andom Ghebreghiorgis says the committee is being terminated and should close after a consultation with the Commission analyst; it references the April and July Quarterly Reports. (Filed 10/07; first surfaced in FEC data in this edition.) Filing

Fair Courts America — Responds to an RFAI dated 09/02/2026 about a $6,809.13 "Advances to be reimbursed" debt forgiven by related entity Restoration of America: the super PAC argues the commercial-debt rules in 11 CFR 116 do not apply because Restoration of America is a social welfare organization, not a commercial vendor. Filing.

Treasurer is Jason Hinton. Filing.

sections.headline: One Large Negative Transaction Reported
paragraphs: Negative amounts in FEC filings represent voided, reversed, or refunded transactions—typically routine corrections, but occasionally part of a larger paper trail. This edition contains one negative transaction exceeding $10,000.
